§6.1 Dot Leader Lines

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-dot-leader-lines · text rule layout

✅ Normative

Dot leaders MUST NOT appear in the output. The label and the value on either side of a leader MUST be kept exactly as printed; the dots themselves produce nothing.

A deliberate exception to verbatim transcription

Everywhere else printed ink survives — see Values Are Verbatim§10.3.3 and Cell Text Fidelity§9.6.3. Dot leaders are the one carve-out: they exist only to guide the eye across a gutter and carry no information.

A dot leader is a run of dots filling horizontal space between a label and a value, most often in a table of contents, a directory or a price list.

Chapter 3 — Reserving  . . . . . . . . . . . . . .  47

Requirements

  • A run of leader dots MUST be removed wherever it is printed: in running text, in a directory line and in a table's stub cell.
  • The label and every value the leader connects MUST be kept, verbatim. The dots go; everything they connect stays.
  • Removing a leader MUST NOT split a label or a value, and a leader MUST NOT be absorbed into either side (no trailing dots on a label, no leading dots on a number).
  • Where a leader separates two values on one line, the values remain on that line, separated by a space.

A dot leader is typesetting, not content: it exists because a label and a number are far apart on the line, and it disappears the moment the text is reflowed. Transcribing it damages what is around it — a run of dots inside a label breaks any string match on that label.

✅ Sample — leader lines with two values at the end

A court directory: each person's line runs a dot leader to an e-mail address in grey and a phone number at the margin. Some lines have no e-mail, so the leader runs straight to the number. This is text, not a table: one line per person, leaders removed, the values separated by spaces. The grey of the e-mail addresses is decoration and is not carried. Heading depths are relative: the page does not show where CALDRIVANE COUNTY sits in the whole directory.
